newsitem.title: EGYPT: Misr Free Shops privatised at 40 pounds.
newsitem.headline: Misr Free Shops privatised at 40 pounds.

text.p: The Egyptian state sold off a majority 66.8 percent stake in Misr Free Shops through the stock exchange on Wednesday at the end of an auction which fixed the sale price at 40.00 pounds a share.
The Capital Market Authority said the state sold 2,337,310 of the shares, more than twice the 1.05 million shares the state had originally offered. The company has 3.5 million shares.

Under the auction procedure for recent Egyptian privatisations, the holding company allocates shares to the highest bidders first and then works its way down the list until it has sold all the shares it wants to sell. The sale price for all shares is the price bid for the last batch allocated.
The minimum price for bids was 32.00 pounds a share.
Misr Free Shops, also known as Egypt Free Shops, has a monopoly on duty-free shops in Egypt.
It made profits for distribution of 13.423 million pounds ($3.95 million) in the financial year 1995/6, which ended on June 30. It forecast the 1996/7 figure would be 15 million.
